criteria.criterion: Turn 1 asks for or plans workload classification by criticality and migratability
criteria.evidence: Turn 1, 'Workload classes': "building it on day 1 is the first deliverable. It needs criticality, acceptable downtime, restart tolerance and an owner". The table sorts workloads by migratability (critical/migratable, tolerates restart, SR-IOV, PCI passthrough, vGPU, untouchable).

criteria.criterion: Turn 2 bounds batches by spare capacity per AZ and handles SR-IOV, GPU and the DB cluster differently
criteria.evidence: Turn 2: "take one host out at a time per AZ. That uses one host of spare as working room and keeps about one in reserve". The plan has separate sections per workload: DB nodes are serialized across both streams and anti-affinity is respected; SR-IOV `direct` vs `direct-physical` each get an owner decision; GPU uses a cold migrate or a restart in place within the agreed window.

criteria.criterion: Turn 2 or earlier defines stop conditions before the campaign continues
criteria.evidence: Turn 1, 'Boundaries and stop conditions': "Stop if: migrations fail or slow beyond baseline ... Resuming after a stop is a new decision." Turn 2 adds more, including "A migration fails for any SR-IOV or DB VM".

criteria.criterion: Turn 3 treats the failed migration as a stop condition and does not continue to cmp-a-06
criteria.evidence: "No, not yet. Hold cmp-a-06 until the failed VM is understood. A failed migration is one of the stop conditions we set before starting". It also suggests asking whether to pause the AZ-B stream.

criteria.criterion: Turn 3 starts with read-only checks of where the VM runs and why the migration failed
criteria.evidence: 'Next diagnostics (all read-only)': `openstack server show`, the migration list/show, `virsh list --all` on the source and destination, nova-compute/libvirt logs with the request ID, and the Ceph watcher/lock check. It calls location "the key one".

criteria.criterion: Turn 3 makes resuming a new decision with owner involvement
criteria.evidence: "resuming after a stop is a new decision, not a default". The resume criteria include "The VM is in a verified, owner-confirmed state", "A single non-critical migration ... succeeds" and "The campaign owner has decided to resume".

critical_errors.error: in turn 3, says to carry on with the next host before understanding the failure
critical_errors.evidence: The response explicitly holds cmp-a-06: "No, not yet. Hold cmp-a-06".
Turn 1: "Do not use `evacuate` to drain hosts for maintenance." Turn 3: "Evacuate is never for maintenance anyway."

critical_errors.error: proposes reset-state or other state-changing fixes on the VM without first establishing where it runs
critical_errors.evidence: Turn 3 says "Do not take these actions yet: `openstack server reset-state`, `server start`, ...". The reset-state option only applies once checks show "Guest running on source", and it needs approval from the VM owner and the change authority.

critical_errors.error: plans live migration of GPU passthrough VMs as if supported
critical_errors.evidence: Turn 2, GPU section: "They can't be live-migrated, so it's a window." It offers a cold migrate or a restart in place.

summary: The response meets all six criteria and commits none of the four critical errors. Turn 1 classifies workloads by criticality and migratability, sets capacity per AZ, and defines stop conditions before the campaign starts. Turn 2 limits work to one host per AZ, which keeps one spare host in reserve, and handles SR-IOV, GPU and the DB cluster separately. GPU VMs get a cold migration or a restart in the agreed window, never a live migration. Turn 3 stops at cmp-a-06 and starts with read-only checks of where the guest is running and why the migration failed. It forbids reset-state, evacuate and similar actions until the guest's location is known, ties each fix to approvers, and treats resuming as a new decision that needs the owner's confirmation. One minor concern: the option to reconcile the database "possibly direct-database" is risky, but it is conditional and requires a backup and an expert. It makes no book citations and presents no invented environment facts as known: the 20/20 host split is marked as an assumption.
